drafts.subject: Fall Remote Research Assistant Inquiry - Integrated Codesign of Printable Robots (Taksh Nahata)
drafts.body:
Dear Dr. Mehta,

I am a dual-enrollment student with 34 college units and a 4.0 GPA, currently based in Folsom, CA. I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the Laboratory for Embedded Machines and Ubiquitous Robots at UCLA as a remote research assistant for the Fall term. Your recent work on the "Integrated Codesign of Printable Robots" deeply resonates with my background in embedded systems and hardware-software co-design. As I reside outside the local driving range, I am seeking a strictly remote opportunity to contribute to your team's advanced research in printable robotics and automated design.

I am seeking a strictly remote volunteer position where I can assist your graduate students by independently handling embedded firmware development, sensor integration, and rapid prototyping validation. Here is how my technical background directly supports your lab's current workload:

• **Custom Short Title (USC AIEA Lab):** I have utilized CARLA autonomous vehicle simulation environments to model physics engine noise and test edge-case failures. This experience in simulation-based validation can assist your lab in testing the robustness of printable robot control algorithms before physical deployment.

• **Custom Short Title (VEX Robotics Team 20000Z):** As Lead Programmer, I developed C++ microcontroller firmware for state estimation using Monte Carlo localization and AprilTags vision processing. This expertise in real-time embedded control and computer vision aligns with the autonomous navigation needs of your integrated codesign projects.

• **Custom Short Title (Ventre Hardware/Medical Startup):** I designed custom PCBs and implemented sensor fusion algorithms for IMUs and biometric data via Bluetooth Low Energy. This hardware abstraction and embedded system design skill set is directly transferable to the embedded control architectures required for your printable robotic systems.

I am available to commit approximately 10 hours per week as a volunteer. I have attached my CV for your review and would welcome the chance to discuss how my remote contributions can support the Laboratory for Embedded Machines and Ubiquitous Robots. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to the possibility of a 10-15 minute Zoom call.

Sincerely,

Taksh Nahata

drafts.subject: Fall Remote Research Assistant Inquiry - XL-VLA and Vision-Language-Action Models (Taksh Nahata)
drafts.body:
Dear Dr. Wang,

I am a student with a dual-enrollment background, having completed 34 college units with a 4.0 GPA. I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the Learning and Vision Lab at UC San Diego as a remote volunteer research assistant. I have been following your work on self-supervised computer vision and video modeling with great admiration. Your recent paper, "XL-VLA: Cross-Hand Latent Representation for Vision-Language-Action Models," particularly resonated with me due to its innovative approach to handling complex manipulation tasks through latent representations. I am eager to contribute to this line of inquiry by supporting your team in advancing vision-language-action integration.

I am seeking a strictly remote volunteer position where I can assist your graduate students by independently handling data pipeline optimization, simulation environment testing, and algorithmic prototyping. Here is how my technical background directly supports your lab's current workload:

• **CARLA Simulation & Anomaly Detection (USC AIEA Lab):** I have experience configuring CARLA autonomous vehicle simulation environments to test edge-case failures and model physics engine noise. This background allows me to rigorously validate the robustness of vision-language-action models under varied and stochastic conditions.

• **C++ Firmware & State Estimation (VEX Robotics Team 20000Z):** As a Lead Programmer, I developed C++ microcontroller firmware integrating AprilTags vision processing with Monte Carlo localization state estimation. This expertise enables efficient implementation of real-time perception modules required for dynamic manipulation tasks.

• **Automated Data Pipelines (Data & Software Engineering):** I have built automated data ingestion pipelines and full-stack Python dashboards for statistical analysis. This skill set supports the large-scale data processing and visualization needs essential for training and evaluating cross-hand latent representation models.

I am available to commit approximately 10 hours per week to this volunteer role. I have attached my CV for your review. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background aligns with the goals of the Learning and Vision Lab during a brief 10-15 minute Zoom call at your convenience.

Sincerely,

Taksh Nahata

drafts.subject: Fall Remote Research Assistant Inquiry - Trajectory Optimization and Legged Locomotion (Taksh Nahata)
drafts.body:
Dear Dr. Righetti,

I am a dual-enrollment student with a 4.0 GPA and 34 college units, and I am writing to express my strong interest in joining the Machines in Motion Laboratory as a remote research assistant this Fall. I have been following your work on legged locomotion with great interest, and I was particularly intrigued by your recent paper, "Hippo: High-Performance Interior-Point and Projection-Based Solver for Generic Constrained Trajectory Optimization." The approach to handling generic constraints in real-time control systems is exactly the kind of rigorous technical challenge I am eager to contribute to.

I am seeking a strictly remote volunteer position where I can assist your graduate students by independently handling software engineering, data pipeline development, and algorithmic prototyping. Here is how my technical background directly supports your lab's current workload:

• **Data Pipeline & Analysis (NYU Machines in Motion Lab):** I have extensive experience building automated data ingestion pipelines and performing statistical analysis using Python. I can assist in structuring the large datasets generated from legged robot simulations and experiments, ensuring clean inputs for your optimization algorithms. My background in full-stack dashboarding allows me to visualize complex trajectory data effectively for the team.

• **Control Algorithm Prototyping (VEX Robotics Team 20000Z):** As a lead programmer, I developed C++ microcontroller firmware and implemented Monte Carlo localization for state estimation. This experience with real-time sensor fusion and state estimation in constrained environments translates well to the practical implementation aspects of trajectory optimization solvers like Hippo.

• **Simulation Environment Support (USC AIEA Lab):** I have worked with CARLA autonomous vehicle simulation environments, focusing on anomaly detection and edge-case failure testing. I can leverage this experience to help stress-test locomotion policies in simulated physics engines, providing valuable feedback on robustness and edge cases for your trajectory planning modules.

I am fully prepared to dedicate approximately 10 hours per week to this volunteer role. I have attached my CV for your review. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my skills might support the Machines in Motion Laboratory. Could we schedule a brief 10-15 minute Zoom call at your convenience?

Best regards,

Taksh Nahata
